name: Network Efficiency Score
description: One number for how healthy the transport company is: on-time rate, load factor, coverage, and profit per route-kilometer folded into a legible 0–100 score with milestone thresholds that gate expansion unlocks. It exists because a tycoon game drowns the player in ledgers, and somebody has to answer 'am I doing well' before the bankruptcy notice does. This component owns only the formula and the thresholds — every input metric is produced elsewhere: schedules and blockages from world.route_network, queues and served passengers from world.passenger_flow, revenue from the economy.earned ledger. It never penalizes directly: a falling score is information, and the carrot is progression.networkMilestoneReached unlocking new vehicle classes and map regions. Publishing the formula's weights is a design stance — a score the player cannot reason about is a weather report, and this genre wants engineering.

inputs.name: weights
inputs.description: Metric weights in the composite score. Public by design — the player optimizes what they can see.

inputs.name: milestoneThresholds
inputs.description: Score values that fire progression.networkMilestoneReached. Spaced so each tier of unlocks arrives just as the current network feels solved.

inputs.name: evaluationIntervalSeconds
inputs.description: How often the score recomputes. Slow enough that the number is a trend line, not a twitchy gauge that punishes a single late bus.

outputs.name: currentScore
outputs.description: Composite 0-100 score. The headline number on the company dashboard.

outputs.name: metricBreakdown
outputs.description: Per-metric contributions to the score, so a falling number always names its cause.
